You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Decrypto Players compete in two teams in Decrypto, with each trying to correctly interpret the coded messages presented to them by their teammates while cracking the codes they intercept from the opposing team. In more detail, each team has their own screen, and in this screen they tuck four cards in pockets numbered 1-4, letting everyone on the same team see the words on these cards while hiding the words from the opposing team. In the first round, each team does the following: One team member takes a code card that shows three of the digits 1-4 in some order, e.g., 4-2-1. They then give a coded message that their teammates must use to guess this code. For example, if the team's four words are "pig", "candy", "tent", and "son", then I might say "Sam-striped-pink" and hope that my teammates can correctly map those words to 4-2-1. If they guess correctly, great; if not, we receive a black mark of failure. Starting in the second round, a member of each team must again give a clue about their words to match a numbered code. If I get 2-4-3, I might now say, "sucker-prince-stake". The other team then attempts to guess our numbered code. If they're correct, they receive a white mark of success; if not, then my team must guess the number correctly or take a black mark of failure. (Guessing correctly does nothing except avoid failure and give the opposing team information about what our hidden words might be.) The rounds continue until a team collects either its second white mark (winning the game) or its second black mark (losing the game). Games typically last between 4-7 rounds. If neither team has won after eight rounds, then each team must attempt to guess the other team's words; whichever team guesses more words correctly wins. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary In this cryptic game of clues and secrecy, your aim is to intercept the opponent team twice without failing your own team twice Turn Structure Each round is split into 8 parts 1) A different Encryptor is designated each turn 2) Encryptors secretly views a Code Card 3) Encryptors writes 3 clues 4) Both teams discuss and write down what they think about the White clues (Excluding White Encryptor, but including Black Encryptor) 5) The White code is revealed. If the Black team is correct, they receive an Interception Token (white token), whilst if they are wrong nothing happens. If the White team is correct, nothing happens, whilst if they are wrong they receive an Miscommunication Token (black token). Parts 4 and 5 are then repeated, with both teams attempting to decipher the Black clues Round End Once both teams have attempted to decipher both codes, the round ends. If one team now has 2 Interception, they win. If one team now has 2 Miscommunication, they lose. If both teams win in the same round, the tokens turn into points, with Interceptions worth +1 and Miscommunication worth -1 to determine the winning team. If both teams are still tied, they can submit their guesses for the 4 words of the other team. If no win/lose condition was triggered, a new round begins. When each new round begins the Code Cards are reshuffled. This means that sequences can repeat within a game. Clue Rules The following are the Encryptor's rules for making their clues : A clue can either be a single word or a phrase Each clue must clearly be separate A clue must only refer to the meaning A clue must NOT refer to inside or private information (e.g., "our dinner last night" or "your sister's favorite animal" for Cow) A clue must NOT use the spelling (e.g. a "C" for Cow) A clue must NOT indicated the number of letters (e.g. a "3" or "Three" for Cow) A clue must NOT indicate the position (e.g. "Tripod" for Cow in third position) A clue must NOT address pronunciation (e.g. "Wow!" to sound like Cow) A clue must NOT be the same word in another language (e.g. "Vache" for Cow) A clue must NOT be a keyword in your code --- nan
community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Extremely slow, dull and boring. Unlike most word and deduction games, it becomes worse with more players as you have to wait even longer to take any action, and the components like transparent covers actually play no role and are there just to artifically raise the price. One of those games where you might accidentally win by doing absolutely nothing due to the bad performance of opposing team.

[Rating: 2/10] If you enjoy playing Codenames but think that it's 40 minutes too short, or the clues are too specific, or the rules too simple, you should try Decrypto once and then never again.

[Rating: 2/10] There are folks who are good at this sort of word deduction thing and folks who aren’t. I am decidedly among the latter. Where Codenames is fairly breezy and light (all the answers are visible), Decrypto is more serious and tense as you try to keep pace with your partner without giving clues away whilst trying to figure out what the hidden words of your opponents are. Like Codenames it’s helpful to know how your partner thinks. Unlike Codenames, it’s also helpful if you know the deck to help narrow down the options of your enemy. Not a fan of deck memorization.

[Rating: 2/10] Seemed fun the first time but as I played more I began to wonder if you could truly be clever with clues - it seemed teams did better by riffing off their own theme continually, obscuring the original word, which felt rather unsatisfying. I'd recommend Wavelength instead.

[Rating: 2/10] jesus God dont make me play this anymore. it's fun and I hate it at the same time.

[Rating: 2/10] My rating is based on the "would I play it again" criteria in BGG's suggested ratings. Mechanically Decrypto is fine, but I personally find it very stressful to play.

[Rating: 2/10] I wish I could take back my pto time used to play this game. I would rather increase shareholder value and be a corporate slave than waste my time creating clues based on inside jokes to guess 50 variations of the order of 4 words. You will keep guessing because each team will base their 'synonyms/descriptions' on words no one else outside of their own circle will understand. I used this technique and it proved very successful. Would I rather do anything else? Yes. Not an enjoyable game, play cards instead.

[Rating: 3/10] Played the prototype at FallCon 30 and was underwhelmed. The rules were muddy and there just wan't much interesting about the game in general. 4 words is too few when you're giving hints for 3 of them each turn; increasing the total number to 5 would at least make it a little more interesting but probably wouldn't be enough to save this one.

[Rating: 3/10] Same problem that Dixit has. Impossible not to give clues that no one else would ever get but your clue receiver. But it doesn't have the pretty art to distract.

[Rating: 3/10] Too long. And too boring. Other games do this way better—like Codenames. And those games aren’t that impressive.

[Rating: 3/10] One aborted play of a very poor devolution of Codenames complete with designed-in excessive AP. Pass!
